newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa plans more Finland flights.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans more Finland flights.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Monday that it planned to offer three more non-stop flights to Finland as part of its winter schedule, which starts on October 26.
The new services will run from Hamburg, Frankfurt and Munich to Helsinki and will increase the number of flights to Finland from Germany to 47 flights a week from 34.

Earlier in the day, Lufthansa announced it was ending its cooperation agreement with Finnair. The two airlines had cooperated in the areas of flight planning, marketing, sales and frequent flyer air miles.

Lufthansa decided to bring the agreement to an end, because the German airline has expanded its cooperation with SAS as part of the Star Alliance agreement. It said it wanted to avoid a conflict of interest in the Scandinavian region.
